source.title: Dynamic Mini-batch SGD for Elastic Distributed Training: Learning in the Limbo of Resources
source.authors: Haibin Lin; Hang Zhang; Yi-Fei Ma; Tong He; Zhi Zhang; Sheng Zha; Mu Li

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: Tests batch-size effects and adaptation on image classification, object detection, and segmentation under elastic distributed training, a setting for the large-batch generalization claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out validation performance for static and dynamically changing batch sizes. It does not test random-label memorization, optimizer comparisons, or the other claim versions.
record.test_reason: The ImageNet experiments directly test V5: all classifiers train for 90 epochs, while static batch size or batch-size schedules vary. Static large batches lose validation accuracy, and adaptive schedules largely preserve it. The record incorrectly says fixed epoch budgets are not tested. Detection and segmentation measure tasks outside V5's stated classifier/language-model scope.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors attribute elastic-training instability mainly to momentum failing to adapt to changing batch sizes. Their gradual learning-rate adjustment stabilizes training and generally achieves accuracy comparable to small-batch static training across three vision tasks. This does not establish that every large batch or schedule preserves accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines elastic, dynamically changing batch sizes and a momentum-compensation learning-rate schedule; it does not test the claim's fixed-epoch large-batch comparison directly.
record.method_sensitivity: Maximum GPU/batch scale (12× versus 16×), static versus randomized GPU schedules, and task/model architecture affect the reported performance. Increasing batch size is more disruptive than decreasing it in the ResNet-50 epoch-20 comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: SSD detection mAP declines from 30.3 to 20.2 with random schedules up to 16× and linear scaling; Dynamic SGD reaches 29.6.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large or changing batches can impair object-detection performance, and gradual learning-rate adaptation can reduce the loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Static large batches reduce FCN segmentation mIoU from 39.48 to 34.69 or 33.65; Dynamic SGD schedules reach 39.34.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large-batch semantic segmentation depends on batch-normalization statistics and batch-size scheduling.

record.problems: The main evidence concerns elastic training schedules, not a controlled fixed-epoch study of batch size. Standard deviations are reported for ResNet-50 random-schedule results, but not for the other reported results.

untested.parts: Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and learned local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning budgets.
Language models, extending the epoch budget, and isolated normalization or regularization remedies. Dynamic schedules do not establish that a constantly large batch can match small-batch accuracy.
Dropout interventions, small-data regimes, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

missing.what: ResNet-50 sudden batch increase from 1K to 12K: linear scaling reaches 76.50/76.54 and Dynamic SGD 76.81/76.81 for changes at epochs 20/70, versus 76.91 at static 1K. Fixed-total-batch controls reach 76.28/75.87 and expose a per-GPU batch-normalization confound.

The batch-size sweep reports static 4K accuracy slightly above 1K, attributed to random variation, followed by deterioration from 8K onward. Dynamic SGD preserves accuracy through 12K but worsens at 16K. Exact plotted values are unavailable in the supplied text.
missing.locator: Section 5.1, Figure 5 and Mini-batch Size Range

missing.what: With weight decay also applied to biases and batch-normalization parameters, static 1K/12K accuracies are 76.89/76.27. Linear scaling reaches 75.03/76.43 for batch increases at epochs 20/70; Dynamic SGD reaches 76.47/76.78. This shows sensitivity to change timing and regularization placement.

record.verdict_notes: All supplied numerical table values match the text. States refer to the batch-size penalty, so preserved accuracy is absent even when it supports V5's adaptation clause. No challenge verdict is warranted because V5 already allows recipe-dependent recovery. Random-schedule maximum batch size is not the batch size used throughout training. Only ResNet-50 random-schedule results report variation across five schedules.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.

Fixed epoch budgets are not directly contrasted as the main intervention; language models are not tested. Experiments vary batch size or GPU schedules and report image, detection, and segmentation validation performance.
Dropout and weight-decay comparisons for held-out error.
Removal of memorized examples and its effect on test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Static 12× and 16× batches for ResNet-50 and Inception V3 on ImageNet, with 90 epochs and linearly scaled learning rates
relationships.reason: R2, R3, R16 and R17 lose 0.57–1.48 accuracy points relative to their 1K references despite the same epoch budget.
relationships.display_finding: Unverified comparisons suggest static larger batches reduced accuracy despite proportional learning-rate scaling.

relationships.condition: MobileNet static large-batch training on ImageNet
relationships.reason: R9 and R10 show only 0.14- and 0.34-point losses, substantially weaker batch sensitivity than the other classifiers.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy losses of 0.14 and 0.34 percentage points were reported, but these batch comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Random batch schedules up to 16× with immediate linear learning-rate scaling
relationships.reason: R6, R13 and R20 lose 0.60–0.90 accuracy points, showing that linear scaling alone does not reliably prevent the penalty.
relationships.display_finding: Unverified results suggest immediate learning-rate scaling failed to prevent accuracy deficits under random batch schedules.

relationships.condition: Adaptive batch schedules: both methods up to 12× and Dynamic SGD up to 16×
relationships.reason: R4, R5, R7, R11, R12, R14, R18, R19 and R21 preserve approximately baseline accuracy within 90 epochs, supporting V5's recipe-adaptation qualification.
relationships.display_finding: Unverified results suggest adaptive batch schedules approximately preserved reference accuracy within the same epoch budget.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Random GPU schedules at maximum scale 16× and static large-batch baselines
reader_labels.reason: Static large-batch results decline, and linear scaling can perform much worse at 16×, while Dynamic SGD generally remains closer to its baseline (R3, R6, R7, R10, R13, R14, R17, R20, R21, R24, R27, R28, R31, R34, R35).
